item: Run records in the storage-events journal: run_export, run_import and run_verify kinds (ten each) for the volume backup, restore and verify, written open and closed at every branch and in a finally net, plus a closed record for each refused start; the slot goes from 90,000 to 115,000 bytes
summary: The Diagnostics zip kept the runs that opened a run journal and nothing for a start refused before one, a worker killed in the middle of a backup, or a backup that ended ok with its summary file not written. storage_events gained three kinds (run_export, run_import, run_verify, ten each, the cap per kind, total counting every run): run_started writes the run OPEN, run_ended closes it at every branch of the three VolumeBackupManager workers with one of eight named outcomes, the seconds and the figures, a finally net closes what no branch did, run_refused records a start refused at the raise (no passphrase, destination unusable, not a folder, already running, named by kind), and export_summary adds summary_error (class only) to a run that ended ok. The sink takes numbers, one flag, class names (shaped like one, 80 characters at most) and keys of fixed tables, never an exception text, a path or a folder name; an AST test reads every hook call, and a marker passphrase planted in every exception is in neither the journal file, the member nor the slot. Free bytes of the destination and of the data folder are read after the run is written open and are absent when unreadable, never 0. The slot budget is 115,000 bytes (widest measured 109,766, ordinary 65,056, a run with every field present 734). 68 tests in the run file, 45 mutants each killed by a named test, ruff total 413. Not recorded, stated: the legacy single-file restore, the folder backup, restore and verify, and the newsletter import write no storage event.
